title: Damayanti
hook: five men stand in the hall with one face, and Damayanti chooses the one with dust on him

segments.voice: Yesterday, Savitri at the banyan, read as devotion, as will and as the divine word. Today, a new woman, and a hall full of gods.
screen: `SHE ACTS WHEN THE WORST NEWS COMES.`

segments.voice: Five men in a row, every one with the same face. That's what Damayanti sees when she walks into her own swayamvara, garland in hand, ready to choose. Four of them are gods wearing the face of the man she loves. One of them is the man. Last year we heard the whole story of Nala and Damayanti, from a golden swan to a long reunion. This time we stay with her: three days, three choices, and the first is made in a hall full of gods.
screen: `FIVE MEN, ONE FACE.` → `FOUR GODS AND A MAN.` → `HER FIRST CHOICE.`

segments.voice: Damayanti is the daughter of King Bhima of Vidarbha. She has chosen Nala in her heart before she ever sees him, because a swan carried his praises to her. Then the gods want her too: Indra, Agni, Varuna and Yama. They make Nala, of all people, carry their offer. She tells him plainly: she is his, and she'll choose him in front of the gods so no blame falls on him. On the day, the gods come as Nala. She can't tell them apart, so she doesn't guess. In her heart she bows to the gods and asks them, by the truth of her promise, to show themselves. And they do. The gods don't sweat. Their eyes don't blink. Their garlands stay fresh, there's no dust on them, their feet don't quite touch the ground, and they cast no shadow. One figure has a shadow, sweat on his skin, dust on him, a garland starting to wilt, and eyes that blink. That's the one she garlands. On one side, gods: perfect, unfading, without a speck on them. On the other, a man who gets dusty and tired, whose flowers die. Every sign that gives him away is a sign of being mortal, and that's exactly how she finds him. She doesn't love him in spite of the dust. The dust is how she knows him. And the gods aren't angry. The story says they bless the couple and give Nala gifts. Perfection, here, steps aside for a person who blinks.
screen: `SHE CHOSE HIM BEFORE SHE SAW HIM` · `SHE ASKS THE GODS BY HER PROMISE` · `NO SWEAT, NO BLINK, NO SHADOW` · `SHE GARLANDS THE ONE WITH DUST`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone close to you, and let one ordinary human sign of theirs come up: how they look when they're tired, a habit, a laugh a little too loud. Not the polished version, the one with dust on; stay with that small sign for a few breaths. If you pray, you can give thanks for them.
Damayanti. The princess of Vidarbha who asked the gods to show themselves, and then chose the one with a shadow.
Your line: Damayanti. Of five faces, she picked the one whose garland wilted. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindus hear Damayanti's story in the Mahabharata's forest book, where the sage Brihadashva tells it to Yudhishthira; it is also retold in later poems, plays and dance across India.

chat.says: How did Damayanti tell the real Nala from the gods?
options: She prayed for the gods to show themselves; Nala was the one with dust, sweat and a shadow.
She asked each one a question only Nala could answer, and only he got it right.
Nala wore the garland she had sent him earlier, so she spotted him at once.
chat.meaning: The gods cast no shadow, don't sweat or blink, and their garlands stay fresh. Nala's signs of being mortal gave him away.

swayamvara.meaning: a gathering where a princess chooses her own husband

Vidarbha.meaning: Damayanti's home kingdom, ruled by her father Bhima

Nala.meaning: the king Damayanti loves and chooses

Agni.meaning: the fire god, one of four gods who wanted her

Varuna.meaning: one of the four gods who came wearing Nala's face
